summary: Implement the frozen canonical catalog/PIM core with tenant-scoped Product and Offer aggregates, forward-only lifecycle and optimistic versions, strict GTIN/SKU invariants, atomic Transactional-Outbox event intent, and a separate generic connector mapping boundary so provider identifiers never enter Core.

impacts.evidence: Products, offers, and connector mappings carry organization/workspace ownership, composite workspace/account/product foreign keys, forced RLS, and tenant-scoped repository queries.
Catalog descriptions are business content and events intentionally retain only identity/version/status/change rather than duplicating full product text; no customer PII is introduced.
Canonical Draft 2020-12 Product, Offer, and connector-mapping contracts establish provider-neutral v1 wire shapes before Task 006/API expansion.

Two versioned catalog events are registered: commerce.catalog.product_changed.v1 and commerce.catalog.offer_changed.v1. Every catalog mutation persists its event intent in the same PostgreSQL transaction.
Remote identity is isolated behind connectors.MappingRepository and connector_entity_mappings. No provider-specific IDs or branches are added to Product/Offer.
Atomic high-risk expand migration 000009 creates Product/Offer/mapping tables, lifecycle/GTIN guards, forced RLS and immutable identity constraints while preserving old readers/writers.

Bounded canonical code/SKU/title/description/remote-ID validation, GS1 check digits, RLS, no hard delete, immutable identities and optimistic versions fail closed against malformed or cross-tenant state.
Catalog lifecycle itself does not grant sensitive publication approval. Task 017 remains the authorization gate for sensitive external writes.

Stable local IDs, monotonic aggregate versions and durable versioned event intents establish deterministic lineage; Task 003 audit remains available to API/application commands without copying remote IDs into Core.
Optimistic versions prevent lost updates, outbox uses stable event IDs, and the separate local/remote mapping table creates the canonical identity bridge needed by Tasks 013/014.
No webhook delivery surface is introduced. Future webhook projections consume canonical catalog events rather than database tables.
Version/change events and mapping versions provide deterministic mutation/reconciliation counters without logging full product payloads or provider credentials.
Migration 000009 is additive. Rollback disables the catalog-aware binary while retaining rows/events; hard deletion is intentionally not an application rollback mechanism.

Tests cover canonical validation, GS1 check digits, forward-only lifecycle, migration/RLS/remote-mapping shape, event/contract fixtures and full repository regression; PostgreSQL smoke exercises atomic domain+outbox behavior.
